text:
Predicates:
Barks(x) ::: x barks
LikesJane(x) ::: Jane likes x
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps
HasLegs(x) ::: x has legs
Terricolous(x) ::: x is terricolous
Kiki(x) ::: x is Kiki

Premises:
Barks(x) → ¬LikesJane(x) ::: If an animal barks, then Jane does not like it
∀x (Dog(x) → Animal(x) ∧ Barks(x)) ::: All dogs are animals that bark
Jumps(x) → Animal(x) ::: If an animal jumps, then it is an animal
HasLegs(x) → Animal(x) ::: If an animal has legs, then it is an animal
Terricolous(x) → HasLegs(x) ::: If an animal is terricolous, then it has legs
(¬Jumps(k) ∧ ¬HasLegs(k)) → (Terricolous(k) ∨ HasLegs(k)) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs

Conclusion:
Terricolous(k)
